Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: 3-day history of diarrhea and vomiting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Diarrhea began 3 days ago, initially watery and now very loose, with at least 4 episodes today
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Diarrhea: started watery → very loose; today ≥4 episodes (lost exact count)

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Vomiting with inability to keep liquids or food down
Last vomiting episode occurred approximately 2 hours ago after breakfast
Subjective fever described as 'running a serious temperature' and 'literally roasting' with no thermometer reading available
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Fever: "running a serious temperature"/"literally roasting"; no thermometer reading

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Periumbilical abdominal pain that is tender to touch
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Abdominal pain: periumbilical/navel area, tender to touch

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Abdominal pain is crampy and intermittent and associated with a strong urge to defecate
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: crampy, intermittent with strong urge to defecate

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports urinating normally and last passed urine about 1 hour ago
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Urine: urinating OK; last passed ~1 hr ago

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is unable to comment on urine color
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: patient unable to comment on color

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Prior to current illness, normal bowel habit was once daily in the morning
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Normal bowel habit: daily x1 in AM prior to illness

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports exposure to a brother with similar gastrointestinal symptoms
Patient reports that others at school are also affected with similar symptoms
Patient attempted treatment with oral rehydration salts about three times per day for 2 days
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Attempts at treatment: oral rehydration salts (salt‑sugar ORS) ~3x/day for 2 days

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Oral rehydration salts have not been tolerated well due to vomiting
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: not tolerated well due to vomiting

Past_Medical_History.content: No past medical or surgical history documented other than menstrual cramps
Past_Medical_History.source_text: PMH/PSH: none documented other than menstrual cramps

Medications.content: Uses ibuprofen occasionally for menstrual cramps

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a graphic designer
Patient lives with her brother and mother
Patient drinks alcohol occasionally, described as 'a pint from time to time'
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: occasional alcohol ("a pint from time to time")

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient does not use recreational drugs
Patient is not sexually active regularly

Assessment.content: Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral or food-borne, with positive household contacts
Assessment.source_text: 1. Acute gastroenteritis — likely viral vs food‑borne; household contacts positive.

Assessment.content: Risk of dehydration due to persistent vomiting and diarrhea, though patient is currently passing urine
Assessment.source_text: 2. Risk of dehydration due to persistent vomiting and diarrhea; currently passing urine.

Assessment.content: Periumbilical crampy abdominal pain associated with bowel urgency
Assessment.source_text: 3. Periumbilical crampy abdominal pain associated with bowel urgency.

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange urgent clinic appointment for assessment of hydration status
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Arrange urgent clinic appointment for clinical assessment of hydration

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange collection of stool sample for microbiological testing for bacterial pathogens
Plan_of_Care.source_text: collection of stool sample for microbiological testing (bacterial pathogens)

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise continuation of oral rehydration solution in very small, frequent sips
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Continue ORS in very small, frequent sips

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise patient to persist with ORS despite intermittent vomiting where possible
Plan_of_Care.source_text: persist despite intermittent vomiting where possible

Plan_of_Care.content: Provide dietary advice to eat bland, simple foods such as toast or biscuits
Advise patient to avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk while symptomatic
Instruct patient to attend A&E urgently if symptoms worsen, if unable to keep fluids down, or if signs of dehydration develop
Plan_of_Care.source_text: If symptoms worsen, cannot keep fluids, or signs of dehydration → attend A&E urgently

Plan_of_Care.content: Plan for appointment booking via support line for scheduling
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Book appointment via support line (patient to be scheduled)

Follow_up_Information.content: Follow-up via urgent clinic appointment to be scheduled through the support line
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Arrange urgent clinic appointment... Book appointment via support line (patient to be scheduled)

Physical_Findings.source_text: No vitals or physical exam documented
No vitals or physical exam documented

Review_of_Systems.content: Genitourinary: patient reports urinating normally with recent urine output about 1 hour ago
Review_of_Systems.source_text: Urine: urinating OK; last passed ~1 hr ago

Review_of_Systems.content: Constitutional: subjective fever with feeling of being very hot
